best_for: Firefox users who want privacy settings and an ad blocker turned on from the first launch, and who will tolerate some broken sites and manual updates.
description:
LibreWolf is a custom version of Firefox built by an independent, largely community-driven project. It is not tied to Mozilla. The team strips out telemetry, data collection and Firefox's experiments, and develops in the open on Codeberg.

Search goes to privacy-minded engines such as DuckDuckGo and SearX. To change a default, put your own settings in a librewolf.overrides.cfg file. It survives updates, and you can copy it to another computer. The docs give ready-made lines for common changes, such as turning Google Safe Browsing back on. They also list test sites, such as the EFF's Cover Your Tracks, to see what your browser reveals, and suggest password managers like Bitwarden and KeePassXC-Browser.

points.title: Firefox with the privacy work done
points.text: LibreWolf follows the latest Firefox release, usually within three days. It comes with uBlock Origin installed, strict tracking protection, HTTPS-Only mode and fingerprint resistance turned on.

points.title: Expect some friction
points.text: Fingerprint resistance forces a light theme, a rounded window size and a UTC time zone, and can break sites that draw on a canvas. Google Safe Browsing and the built-in password manager are off.

points.title: Streaming needs a switch
points.text: DRM playback is off by default, so Netflix, Disney+ and Hulu will not play until you enable DRM content in Settings, General.

points.title: Updates are on you
points.text: LibreWolf has no built-in auto-update except on macOS. On Windows, the installer can set up the separate WinUpdater on a schedule, or you can update through winget, Scoop or Chocolatey.

points.title: Sync works if you turn it on
points.text: Firefox Sync can be enabled and encrypts data before upload. You can also host the older Sync server yourself.

points.title: Versions kept here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 201 versions, with x64 and Arm64 installers that install machine-wide. macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon) and Linux list only the current release. The Flatpak is verified on Flathub as published by the LibreWolf Community.
